DN02 is a medical diagnosis code representing recurrent and persistent blood in the urine (hematuria) [^src1]. Within the Danish healthcare system, this code plays a specific role in monitoring the quality of care for patients with [[atrieflimren]] [^src2]. Specifically, DN02 is utilized as part of a broader set of diagnostic codes to calculate the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] among this patient population [^src3].

The code is documented in the annual reports for the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) [^src1]. In these reports, DN02 is grouped alongside other codes to capture bleeding events in different organ systems. For instance, while codes like [[di60|DI60]] through [[ds066|DS066]] track intracranial bleeding, and [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] through [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] track gastrointestinal bleeding, DN02 is categorized under urinary tract and pulmonary bleeding, alongside codes such as [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]] [^src1]. This standardized coding allows for consistent data collection and regional comparison of clinical outcomes across Denmark [^src2].
